newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IPC Corp says to focus on margins.
newsitem.headline: IPC Corp says to focus on margins.

text.p: IPC Corp Ltd chairman Patrick Ngiam said on Tuesday the group planned to focus on improving its profit margins and to concentrate on volume sales.
Ngiam was speaking at a briefing to announce the personal computer group's interim results.
The firm said earlier net profits fell 85 percent to Singapore $5.32 million for the six months to June 30. Turnover for the first half fell to S$738.4 million against S$833.8 million previously.
It said it made an extraordinary gain of S$19.3 million from the sale of its stake in Groupe Bull
"We will render every effort to stay above the zero level (for the second half)," Ngiam said.
He said the company's inventory at the end of the first six months of 1996 was worth S$200 million.
Ngiam said IPC would have to ride out the difficult conditions in the personal computer industry and aimed to enter 1997 with its focus on five core business areas.
These were in information technology products, interactive media services, original equipment manufacturing, distribution and telecommunications.
He said the group's non-computer business, which included telecommunications, was expected to contribute to the bottom line only from 1998.
